task_3_j2_heal_01_catalog_cascade.verdict: VERIFIED — catalog-side allergen updates do NOT mutate frozen composition_snapshot / allergens_snapshot on existing orders; KDS cache invalidates for NEW orders via Q9-S1 sync.
cascade: 1. Admin updates items.allergen_flags via /admin/items/{id}/update (admin UI editor — future, per LeCayenneAllergenSeeder docblock:41-43). I.2-HEAL-02 ItemUpdated event (per task spec reference) dispatches OrderCreated-like envelope.
2. Q9-S1 cross-surface sync (MEMORY START HERE bullet 1, 0-60s → ~1s mesuré empiriquement): kiosk catalog cache invalidates, POS catalog refreshes, KDS sees new flag in subsequent orders.

3. EXISTING orders: composition_snapshot frozen at FrontendOrderService.php:442 (per K.1 cascade); allergens_snapshot hydrated at :455 via OrderItemAllergenSnapshot::hydrate (per K.1 files_examined). Both are SNAPSHOT columns on order_items — once written, they reflect the state at order creation. Admin item update has zero retroactive effect on cards already on the KDS board.

4. NF525 invariant preserved: closed-order audit trail immutable. Wave Q-4 migration explicitly excludes DELIVERED/CANCELED/REJECTED/RETURNED from the open-orders clear (database/migrations/2026_05_20_120000_clear_fake_allergen_data_wave_q4.php:36-38) — same discipline applies to admin updates (no overwrite path exists).

5. KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService.php:389-426 line-dedupe relies on sha1(normalizeAllergensForHash(allergens_snapshot)) — two lines with same item but different snapshots stay distinct on the card. Catalog-side flag change creates NEW orders with NEW snapshot; existing-order lines keep their pre-change snapshot. Chef sees the legacy allergen state for the in-flight ticket, and the new state from the next-ticket-onwards. By design — chef should not have the rug pulled mid-prep.
task_3_j2_heal_01_catalog_cascade.edge_case_chef_perspective: If chef stands at KDS while admin retroactively flags 'arachides' on an item, the in-flight ticket's pill / border / per-line ⚠ does NOT light up — because the composition_snapshot is frozen. Chef preparing that ticket would not know. This is correct from NF525 audit-trail perspective, but operationally requires the new flag to take effect on the NEXT order. ACCEPTABLE per task spec — 'composition_snapshot frozen → old allergen flags stay'. Owner-decision footprint: if real chef-confirmed allergen data arrives, the FIRST in-flight order at that moment is still rendered with the pre-change state. Mitigation if needed: print a manager-only banner 'Allergen catalog updated at HH:MM — verify in-flight orders' (NOT implemented at HEAD, V1.0.X backlog if owner deems necessary).

spec_vs_code_color_divergence_finding.evidence: Task spec NOUVELLE=yellow/blue, EN COURS=orange. Code NOUVELLE=white/gray (kdsState.js:88), EN COURS=blue (:89). Orange is reserved for ALLERGEN signal at card-chrome level (#F97316 border + #EA580C pill). Yellow is reserved for CASH-PENDING (#FEF3C7 + #92400E + #F59E0B). Green for PRÊT and gray for DONE match. The implemented palette is semantically coherent (each color has a single meaning: orange=allergen-danger, yellow=cash-wait, blue=in-prep, green=ready, gray=neutral/new/done) — REASONABLE; spec was a high-level approximation not pixel-accurate.
spec_vs_code_color_divergence_finding.recommendation: If owner wants spec-exact colors: change NEW theme to {bg:#FEF3C7, dot:#F59E0B} (yellow) AND change PREPARING theme to {bg:#FED7AA, dot:#EA580C} (orange) — BUT this collides with cash-pending yellow AND allergen orange, breaking 1s-glance semantic separation. Better outcome: keep implemented palette and update task-spec doc to reflect actual colors. No code change required.

task_6_multi_station_banner_j_adv_8_ux_0.j_adv_8_ux_04_assessment: AT HEAD: per-station-bump-state risk SURFACED to chef explicitly via top banner + redundant hover tooltip. Chef CAN dismiss the top banner (UX comfort) but cannot dismiss the hover tooltip (always-on insurance). V1 Le Cayenne LOCAL = single physical KDS screen (per L.4 deployment_context_discriminator + CLAUDE.md §6) → operational risk = ZERO (one chef, one screen, no fanout). V2 SaaS multi-restaurant = real concern: each restaurant's KDS could have multiple kitchen screens, bumping order #42 on station A doesn't update station B (no WebSocket fanout per Wave V 2026-05-21 immediate-PATCH design — the PATCH itself broadcasts via OrderStatusChanged but the OPTIMISTIC local-only 'Prêt confirmed' state isn't shared). V2 mitigation path: subscribe each KDS to OrderStatusChanged event for cross-station consistency (already broadcast per K.1.2). NOT BLOCKING for V1.

findings.title: Canonical v2 KdsOrderCard.vue .kds-card__allergen-pill is non-clickable — modal unreachable from v2 grid
findings.summary: KdsAllergensModal opens via openAllergensModal(order) which is bound to <button class='kds-allergens-badge' v-on:click=...> in the legacy 4-lane KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue (lines 307/496/667/844). The canonical v2 KdsOrderCard.vue:46-56 renders .kds-card__allergen-pill as a <span> (no @click), so chefs using the v2 grid (default since Wave Z 5C 2026-05-16) cannot click-through to the detailed modal. The pill IS visually present (role='alert' aria-live='assertive'), and the per-line ⚠ icon + per-line 'allergen' codes block (KdsOrderLine.vue:76-81) DO surface the allergen codes inline on each card body — so the information is NOT lost; the modal is just unreachable from the v2 UI. Chef in v2 reads codes inline; chef in legacy 4-lane gets click-to-expand modal experience.
findings.evidence: KdsOrderCard.vue:46-56 <span class='kds-card__allergen-pill' role='alert' aria-live='assertive'> — no @click handler. KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:307 legacy <button class='kds-allergens-badge' @click='openAllergensModal(order)'>.
findings.recommendation: OPTION A (minimal): convert .kds-card__allergen-pill from <span> to <button type='button' @click.stop='$emit("open-allergens", order)'> + bubble to KdsV2Grid → parent. ~6 lines. OPTION B (no-op): document that v2 surfaces allergen detail INLINE per-line (.kds-line__allergen-block:76-81 lists codes via allergenLabel + joinedCodes) and modal is legacy-fallback-only — sufficient for chef-rush UX. Owner-decision. Recommend OPTION B for V1 since per-line codes are already on-card; modal click-through is convenience not necessity.

findings.title: Modal focus-trap single-focusable edge case
findings.summary: When allergens modal contains only the Close button (no other interactive elements), onAllergensModalKeydown:1647-1677 line 1663 preventDefault's Tab on focusables.length<2 — focus is stuck on Close. WCAG-compliant (focus trapped) but slightly unusual UX. Adding tabindex='0' to .kds-allergens-modal-content would give a logical 'modal body' focus stop.
findings.recommendation: Future polish: add tabindex='0' role='document' to .kds-allergens-modal-content. Not blocking V1.

findings.title: Multi-station bump-state not synced across KDS screens (J-ADV-8 UX-04)
findings.summary: When chef bumps order #42 on KDS station A, the optimistic local state ('Prêt confirmed') is not pushed to station B. The PATCH itself broadcasts OrderStatusChanged per K.1.2 cascade — so station B sees the eventually-consistent state via the server event — but there's no per-station 'just-bumped' UX flair sync. V1 Le Cayenne single-station = zero risk. V2 multi-restaurant SaaS where kitchens may have 2+ KDS stations = real concern; documented per Wave Polish + K.4 + task spec.
findings.evidence: KdsV2Grid.vue:296-318 onCtaTap dispatches change-status event but no cross-station optimistic broadcast. KdsStatusBanner.vue:114-120 + KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:41 wire 'LOCAL' banner explicitly to chefs.
findings.recommendation: V1: NO ACTION — banner + per-key tooltip already disclose limitation. V2: subscribe each KDS to OrderStatusChanged for cross-station consistency OR station-bound order routing. Add to V1.0.X / V2 cloud-prep backlog.

verdict: GREEN — Le Cayenne V1 LOCAL ship-ready for allergen + status badges + cash-pending + multi-station banner. All 7 task dimensions verified at HEAD. 5 findings surfaced: 3 INFO/P3 (color spec drift + non-clickable v2 pill + modal single-focusable edge), 1 P2 V2-BACKLOG (multi-station cross-screen sync — V1 single-station immune), 1 INFO FIC compliance gate documented (production-France ship blocker — owner-known, V1.0.2 backlog per MEMORY). NF525 closed-order immutability VERIFIED preserved by Wave Q-4 migration discipline. Chef-rush 1s glance discipline ACHIEVED via triple signal (border + pill + per-line icon) with semantic color separation (orange=allergen-only, yellow=cash-only, blue=preparing, green=ready, gray=neutral).
verdict_rationale: Wave Q-4 fake-allergen retraction is bulletproof via 3-layer defense (seeder NOOP + idempotent migration + e2e regression spec) and respects NF525 immutability (closed-order snapshots excluded from clear). Allergen rendering pipeline uses 5 layered guards (per-card pill v-if + card border override + card stripe override + per-line icon v-if + per-line block) all sourced from defensive filtered+deduped+sorted helper functions (kdsAllergens.js). Cash-pending badge is fully wired backend-to-frontend with 3-layer click/keyboard/server gate. Status badge palette is semantically coherent though diverges from task-spec color descriptions (INFO-level documentation drift). Multi-station banner is active by default + dismissible per-device + reinforced by always-on per-key tooltip — V1 single-station Le Cayenne LOCAL has zero operational risk; V2 SaaS multi-station documented as P2 backlog. KdsAllergensModal a11y discipline complete (focus trap + return focus + Escape + backdrop click + ARIA dialog markup + i18n parity across fr/en/ar). L4 browser compat resolved via CLAUDE.md §6 deployment context (KDS Chromium primary, Safari/Firefox is admin-surface only). FIC compliance gate documented in seeder docblock — owner-known production-France blocker, NOT a V1 LOCAL blocker.
